subject: geography

moments.title: UN declares the Decade
moments.body: 1 March 2019: the UN General Assembly proclaims 2021-2030 the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, led by UNEP and FAO. Goal: prevent, halt and reverse the degradation of ecosystems worldwide.
moments.takeaway: Restoration moves from the margins of conservation to a central UN initiative — recognising that protecting remaining habitat is insufficient.

moments.title: Decade officially launched
moments.body: 5 June 2021 (World Environment Day): the Decade is officially launched. Targets include restoring 350 million hectares of degraded land — an area larger than India. Linked to the Bonn Challenge (2011) and the New York Declaration on Forests (2014).
moments.takeaway: Restoration is positioned alongside climate mitigation: restored ecosystems sequester carbon, support biodiversity and provide ecosystem services.

moments.title: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
moments.body: 19 December 2022: 196 parties agree the '30 by 30' target — protect 30% of land and sea by 2030. Restoration commitments are central. The agreement also targets reductions in pollution and invasive species, and increases in financial flows for biodiversity.
moments.takeaway: Biodiversity now has a target framework comparable to the climate '1.5°C' goal — though enforcement and finance remain contested.

now.title: From pledges to projects
now.body: Major projects within the Decade: the African-led Great Green Wall (a 8,000 km belt across the Sahel), Pakistan's '10 Billion Tree Tsunami', UK rewilding initiatives (Knepp, Wild Ennerdale). The 30 by 30 target faces particular challenges over indigenous land rights and 'paper parks' (protected areas without effective management).
now.open_questions: Can restoration scale fast enough? Tree planting is the most visible form, but reforestation can backfire (monocultures, wrong species, displacing communities). 'Natural climate solutions' face the same risks of greenwashing as carbon offsets.

reflection: International environmental targets have shifted from 'protect what's left' to 'restore what's been lost'. The Decade on Restoration is a recognition that survival of ecosystems requires active intervention at scale — and that the political and financial machinery to do this is still being built.
